messages:
Mia Chen: Heads up — noticed a ~30m window of elevated GPU contention in eu-central-1 at ~15:32 UTC, several dedicated pools reported throttling and increased queue times. Opening thread to capture timeline + learnings.
Raj Patel: Which pools? Dedicated or shared?
Mia Chen: Primarily dedicated-pool-eu-prod-* (3 hosts), plus one autoscaled burst group. Shared serving nodes unaffected.
Leo Alvarez: I pulled metrics — GPU util on those hosts spiked to 97-99% and memory rose from 68% -> 93% over ~12 minutes. No hard OOM kills but lots of allocation retries and kernel timeouts.
Sara Kim: Any network errors reported? Could token-stream backlog cause longer-lived KV cache leading to memory growth?
Mia Chen: Network looks clean based on VPC flow logs. KC (KV cache) hit rate for affected routes dropped 10% when model variant fallback kicked in.
Oncall Bot: ALERT: ded-pool-eu-prod-3 latency > SLO for 184s, auto-throttle engaged.
Raj Patel: Did rollout happen around that time? Model push or config change?
Leo Alvarez: No deployment jobs in that 30m window per deploy-bot. There was, however, a scheduled batch eval from research hitting the same models (heavy context size).
Mia Chen: Confirmed — research eval job #r-2027-03-08-09 used long-context sequences (16k) and targeted the dedicated pools for GPU affinity. It started ~15:27 UTC.
Sara Kim: That explains memory rise. Those long contexts keep KV cache hot; runtime doesn't evict aggressively when affinity pins requests to same hosts.
Raj Patel: Why did eval land on dedicated-prod hosts? We have affinity rules to route evals to dev/dedicated-test pools.
Mia Chen: Ops routing config had a stale tag mapping; the eval job used an older scheduler label and fallback hit prod pools.
Leo Alvarez: Logs show allocator fragmentation increased due to repeated large batch allocations from eval — fragmentation plus high util meant no headroom for normal traffic.
Oncall Bot: ACTION: temporarily shift research evals to ded-test and scale temp burst capacity (+2 gpus) — done at 15:40 UTC. Latency restored to 95th SLO by 15:44.
FinOps Bot: Cost note: those extra burst GPUs added ~4 GPU-hours billed to research org.
Mia Chen: Root cause summary: mis-tagged eval job + affinity routing + long-context evals caused sustained memory and kernel stalls on a small subset of dedicated hosts, leading to throttles and elevated latency. No customer-facing errors but elevated tail latency.
Sara Kim: Mitigations taken: 1) re-tagging check in scheduler (hotfix) 2) add preflight that prevents evals with context >8k from landing on prod-dedicated pools 3) autoscaler tweak to reserve 10% buffer GPU for prod pools when KV cache pressure detected.
Raj Patel: Action items + owners: - Scheduler tagging validation: Raj - due EOD today. - Preflight eval constraint: Mia + Research lead - PR by tomorrow. - Autoscaler reserve: Leo - RFC in 48h. - Cost recovery guidance: Finance (cc @FinOps) to decide billing for ad-hoc burst.
Mia Chen: Also adding a runtime metric alert for "persistent allocator fragmentation" (threshold: >3min continuous + >80% memory) so we can catch this earlier.
Leo Alvarez: Will add a small telemetry export (histogram of free contiguous memory) to help tune GC/eviction heuristics.
Sara Kim: Postmortem note: consider a scheduler policy that prefers model-shape awareness (context-length) when assigning affinity.
Mia Chen: TL;DR — incident contained by shifting evals + burst capacity; root cause was scheduling/tagging mismatch plus long-context evals exhausting headroom on a tiny subset of dedicated GPUs. Action items assigned. Closing thread once owners ack. :white_check_mark:
Raj Patel: Acked.
Leo Alvarez: Acked.
Sara Kim: Acked.
FinOps Bot: Noted for chargeback review.
